content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In Christian teaching, wind most commonly symbolizes the Holy Spirit — the invisible, sovereign, life-giving breath/Spirit of God. The link is built into the biblical languages themselves: Hebrew 'ruach' and Greek 'pneuma' each mean wind, breath, and spirit, so interpreters routinely treat wind as the standing image of the Spirit's unseen but powerful activity in creation, regeneration, and empowerment.","primary_basis":["John 3:8 — 'The wind blows where it wishes... so it is with everyone born of the Spirit' (Jesus' explicit wind/Spirit analogy in the new-birth discourse)","Acts 2:2-4 — the sound 'like a mighty rushing wind' at Pentecost accompanying the outpouring of the Holy Spirit","Ezekiel 37:9-14 — the breath/wind (ruach) summoned to give life to the dry bones, interpreted as God's Spirit","Genesis 1:2 — the ruach of God hovering over the waters, widely read as Spirit/wind/breath in creation","Genesis 2:7 — God breathing the breath of life into Adam","John 20:22 — Jesus breathing on the disciples, saying 'Receive the Holy Spirit'"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Wind as an instrument or image of divine judgment and God's destructive/purging power (the east wind, scattering chaff, the whirlwind of wrath).","basis":["Jeremiah 4:11-12","Hosea 13:15","Exodus 14:21 (east wind at the Red Sea)","Psalm 1:4 (wicked as chaff the wind drives away)","Isaiah 40:7","Jonah 1:4; 4:8"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Wind as instability, changeableness, or false teaching — being 'tossed' or 'blown about' as a figure for doubt and doctrinal fickleness.","basis":["Ephesians 4:14 ('tossed to and fro... by every wind of doctrine')","James 1:6 (the doubter like a wave driven by the wind)","Jude 12 ('clouds without water, carried about by winds')"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Wind as the transience, emptiness, or vanity of human life and effort ('chasing after wind', life as a passing breath).","basis":["Ecclesiastes 1:14 and repeated 'striving after wind' refrain","Psalm 103:15-16","Psalm 78:39","Job 7:7"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Wind/storm as theophany — the medium or accompaniment of God's presence and power when He appears or speaks (though sometimes pointedly NOT the locus of His presence).","basis":["Job 38:1 (God answers out of the whirlwind)","1 Kings 19:11 (great wind, 'but the LORD was not in the wind')","2 Kings 2:11 (Elijah taken up in a whirlwind)","Psalm 104:3-4 (God rides on the wings of the wind; makes winds His messengers)","Nahum 1:3"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Winds/storms as trials, adversity, or hostile forces that test faith — often with Christ's authority over the wind demonstrating His deity.","basis":["Matthew 7:25-27 (winds beating on the house)","Mark 4:37-41 and Matthew 14:24-32 (Jesus stilling the wind)","Revelation 7:1 (four winds held back)"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"Wind is a genuinely polysemous biblical image, and responsible commentators insist context governs its sense in any given passage. Nevertheless, when Christians speak of what wind 'symbolizes,' the dominant, catechetically standard answer is the Holy Spirit, anchored by John 3:8 and Acts 2 and reinforced by the ruach/pneuma wordplay. The judgment, instability/false-doctrine, transience, and theophany readings are all well attested in commentaries and preaching but function as context-specific senses rather than the default symbolic identification."}
